solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poor prospect filmed at a distance

definitions.meaning: a bet or venture with little chance of success
a camera take made from far away, showing a wide scene

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an outsider unlikely to win, and a cinema take framed from far off.

clue.text: Greek character ushers doctor into car

indicators.note: into says the doctor's letters go inside the car's name

parts.note: the Lada is a Russian make of car
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A Greek man shows a physician into a waiting vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ushers' is a link word painting the scene; 'into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, so a Greek character in the letter sense.

clue.text: Kelly eats rats, etc? Don't fret!

indicators.note: eats means one name swallows the other piece, putting it inside

parts.note: Ned Kelly was a famous Australian outlaw
rats and similar pests are vermin

explanation.surface: Someone named Kelly dines on rodents, and another tells them not to worry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom telling someone not to worry about something, same as don't fret.

clue.text: Waif to settle outside Reading

indicators.note: outside says the verb's letters go around the abbreviation

parts.note: to settle somewhere is to stay
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs of schooling

explanation.surface: A homeless child is told to find a home beyond the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a town west of London, but here it is the R of the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic).
explanation.definitionFit: A waif is a homeless child, and a stray is a person or animal without a home.

clue.text: It produces fruit or veg

parts.note: taken as written
chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: Something that grows either fruit or vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plantation of fruit trees, so it is something that yields fruit.

clue.text: Few deface the church

parts.note: to scar something is to disfigure or deface it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Only a handful of vandals spoil the church building.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce describes something in short supply, so few are to be found.

clue.text: Trick nurse's rival

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
to nurse something is to tend it, so one who nurses is a tender

explanation.surface: A nurse's competitor plays a dirty trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a competitor for a title or prize, which makes them a rival.

clue.text: Crest of a bird with part missing

indicators.note: missing says the named piece is removed from the bird's name

parts.note: the partridge is a game bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: Describing the feathery crest of a bird that has lost a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crest' looks like part of the bird, but it is the definition: a hill crest.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the long narrow top of a hill or roof, its crest.

clue.text: Despite that, gets game bird

parts.note: a game or sporting contest is an event
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Even so, someone wins a game bird such as a pheasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game bird' reads as one phrase, but splits into game and bird; 'gets' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning nevertheless, in spite of what has just been said.

clue.text: Nonconformist has Jagger about to swear

indicators.note: about means the singer's first name goes around the verb

parts.note: Mick Jagger is the singer of the Rolling Stones
to aver is to declare firmly, to swear

explanation.surface: A rebel has the Rolling Stones singer about to curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A maverick is an independent-minded person who refuses to follow the crowd.

clue.text: Nervous when working with creep

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
to edge is to move slowly and carefully, to creep

explanation.surface: Someone feels anxious working alongside an unpleasant person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creep' looks like a noun for a nasty person, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being tense and irritable, so nervous.

clue.text: What the smart admirer presses

parts.note: a well-dressed person irons a garment, while a wooer urges his courtship

explanation.definitionFit: A suit is both clothing a smart dresser irons and a courtship an admirer pursues.

clue.text: Amateur work about Romeo and model is obscene

indicators.note: about says the home-improvement letters go around the others

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home improvement by amateurs
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Model T was an early Ford car

explanation.surface: A homemade project depicting Romeo and a model is indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty is a common synonym for obscene or smutty.

clue.text: A maiden was not accustomed to hold me for pleasure

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: to hold means the old contraction takes the next word inside it

parts.note: usen't is an old contraction of used not, as in was not accustomed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman who wasn't used to it kept me entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement is enjoyment or entertainment, so pleasure.

clue.text: Partisan located outside Indian capital

indicators.note: outside says the verb's letters go around the capital letter

parts.note: based means situated or located

indicators.note: capital means the capital letter, the first one, of the next word

explanation.surface: A guerrilla fighter based just beyond Delhi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian capital' wants to be Delhi; it is just the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Partisan means prejudiced in favour of one side, which is to be biased.

clue.text: A nurse set out for Bordeaux

indicators.note: out means the letters are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nurse lays out a bottle of claret.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France, an example.

clue.text: Swimmer thanks key staff

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you
D is a musical key
a staff is a long stick or pole

explanation.surface: A swimmer thanks key personnel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key staff' reads as important employees but splits into key and staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a young frog that lives and swims in water.

clue.text: Typically Nero gave a new production

indicators.note: a new production restages something, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Usually, the emperor Nero staged a fresh show.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually or as a rule, so typically.

clue.text: Artist raised brackets for lighting

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters read upward, backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
clamps and brackets both hold things in place

explanation.surface: A painter puts up brackets to hang lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Arc lamps are electric lights using an arc between electrodes, a kind of lighting.

clue.text: Soldier has question for the defence

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, so a soldier
to question something is to doubt it

explanation.surface: A soldier has doubts about the case for the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the defence' sounds legal; the defence is a fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small fort or outwork built for defence.

clue.text: City destroyed in attempt to retain love

indicators.note: to retain means the attempt holds the next letter inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A ruined city attempts to keep its love alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the ancient city sacked by the Greeks, according to legend.

clue.text: Mad Hatter's a menace

indicators.note: mad means the letters are sent crazy into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter from Alice is a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a danger or menace.

clue.text: Willing to examine a note

parts.note: to test is to examine
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to look at a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' looks like keen, but means having made a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Testate describes someone who has made a valid will, so willing in a legal sense.

clue.text: Snakes and their associates decapitated

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: snakes and ladders is a board game, so ladders are the snakes' partners

explanation.surface: Snakes and their friends are beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Snakes and ladders is a children's board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Adders are venomous snakes, so an example of the definition.

clue.text: Degenerate corrupted? Oh 'e's cruel

indicators.note: corrupted means the letters are spoilt into a different order

explanation.surface: A Cockney complains that someone corrupt is cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecherous means lustful, and a degenerate is morally depraved.

clue.text: Many an unidentified writer in the ministry

definitions.note: a phrase for one who serves in the church

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a big number
anon is short for anonymous, an author who is not named

explanation.surface: Lots of anonymous authors work in government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ministry' suggests government; it is the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy at a cathedral, so serving in the church.

clue.text: Requirement, they say, for massage

indicators.note: they say tells the solver to go by sound, not spelling

parts.note: a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: Someone says they need a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work dough or muscles, a form of massaging.

clue.text: Criticise strike

definitions.meaning: to run something down or find fault with it

explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses: to disparage something and to hit something.

clue.text: Small car's no good in heavy industry

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A compact car is useless in heavy industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mining is extraction of coal and ores, an example of heavy industry.

clue.text: Boats in ruins before time? Treachery!

indicators.note: before says the first piece comes ahead of the second
in ruins means the letters are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Ships wrecked before their time: deliberate betrayal!
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate destruction by an insider, a kind of treachery.

clue.text: South American breeding ground is most rational

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South America
a nest is where birds breed

explanation.surface: A South American breeding site is the most sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanest is the superlative of sane, most sensible.

clue.text: Holiday touring Asian city is not responsible

indicators.note: touring means the break goes around, encircling the city

parts.note: a recess is a break or holiday
KL is Kuala Lumpur, capital of Malaysia

explanation.surface: A holiday touring an Asian city is irresponsible.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless means heedless of danger, and so not responsible.
